subject: Is that really your friend?
preheader: A cloned-account scam, locking your email, and AI that sharpens a resume.
intro: A good week to protect the account that matters most.

sections.label: Scam of the week
sections.title: A second friend request from someone you already know
paragraphs: You get a new friend request from someone you're already friends with, and then a message asking for help, money, or a code. Their account was copied.
bullets: Contact them another way, like a phone call, and ask if they really sent it.
Don't send money or codes through messages.
Report the fake account in the app, and let your friend know.

sections.label: Tip of the week
sections.title: Lock your email first
paragraphs: Your email can reset every other account, so protect it first. Turn on two-step verification, which is also called two-factor authentication.
bullets: Open your email account's security settings. For Google, go to myaccount.google.com and choose Security.
Find "2-Step Verification" or "Two-factor authentication" and follow the prompts.
Keep any backup codes it gives you somewhere safe at home.

sections.label: AI trick of the week
sections.title: Tidy up a resume bullet
paragraphs: Paste a few lines from your resume and ask for clearer wording.
sections.prompt: Here are three bullets from my resume. Make them clearer and stronger without making anything up: [paste them here]
sections.note: Only keep what is true, and read every line before you use it.
